summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent break-in at its national crime database, NCIC. Trump called it 'not good,' and the FBI has not commented or named who did it. The USDA is still recovering from a separate cyber incident. No official source links the two.

events.title: FBI probes suspected breach of its national crime database
events.impact: Police use NCIC to check warrants and missing-person records. Reports do not say if it went down or if records were taken or changed. AP, which cites a person familiar with the matter, says no sign yet of a link to recent outages.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. The FBI declined to comment Saturday. CNN, NBC, AP and Fox cite unnamed sources. Nothing reported links it to the September FBI jobs portal breach by ShinyHunters.

events.title: USDA cyber incident disrupts farm payment and loan systems
events.impact: Farm loan, payment and conservation tools were disrupted. An official expected most systems back Friday, with work over the weekend. He said no personal data was lost. I found no newer update.
events.stated_cause: A USDA under secretary called it a cyberthreat. Staff reset database passwords. As of Friday night USDA had not named an attacker or said how it happened.

events.title: Tankers hit near Hormuz as Iran tightens control of shipping
events.impact: New Saturday: British maritime authorities reported two tankers hit by unidentified projectiles. Iran says another tanker hit a mine. The US is blockading Iranian ports. Iran also plans rolling blackouts at home.
events.stated_cause: Iran says it is controlling the strait. The US calls its strikes defensive. Iran's mine claims are mostly unverified, though some tanker hits are confirmed by a British monitor.

events.title: Bitcoin steady near 60K USD after a week of losses
events.impact: Price check: CoinGecko 60,629 (+4.8% in 24h, -6.7% in 7 days), Coinbase 60,172, Bitget 60,181. Prices agree. A CoinMarketCap snippet near 59K was a week old. No exchange outage found.
events.stated_cause: No technical or attack cause reported. Earlier reports tie the drop to the stock selloff and forced selling in crypto futures.

events.title: US stocks fall sharply; Dow and S&P 500 in correction
events.impact: Friday close from last run: Nasdaq 22,617.73 (-5.28%), S&P 500 6,910.39 (-3.7%), Dow 48,147.33 (-1.93%). US markets are closed until Monday, so no recheck. No trading halts found.
events.stated_cause: Reports cite worry about AI spending, with Nvidia down 14%. No technical fault or cyber attack is reported.

events.title: CISA adds four actively exploited flaws to its catalog
events.impact: Covers SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway, VMware vCenter and Apache Roller. Federal agencies must fix them. This is a routine notice, not an emergency directive.
events.stated_cause: CISA says it has evidence of active exploitation. It names no attacker and does not link the flaws to the USDA or FBI incidents.

events.title: Cloudflare status page shows degraded performance
events.impact: Cloudflare's status feed lists Sites and Services as degraded, last changed 01:11 UTC Nov 22. I saw no wire report of a wide outage.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. Cloudflare gave no cause in the data I saw.

events.title: Undersea cable fault slows internet in Pakistan
events.impact: Pakistan's telecom authority reported a SEA-ME-WE 5 fault offshore with slow service. I found no new update in this run.
events.stated_cause: Unknown and under investigation. Sabotage claims on social media are unverified.

events.title: Xsolla game payment service shows a major outage
events.impact: Xsolla's own status page showed a Pay Station major outage, per trackers. One tracker still lists Pay Station as a warning. Some game purchases may fail. Steam had checkout complaints earlier, but nobody has linked the two.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. Xsolla's posted note says only that it is investigating a payment processing issue. Valve has said nothing.

events.title: Microsoft explains Nov 12 global Microsoft 365 outage
events.impact: Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams and Copilot were disrupted for almost 24 hours. Microsoft gave its full cause on Saturday.
events.stated_cause: Microsoft says a months-old software bug was triggered after Teams traffic moved to Exchange servers with less capacity. It says it was not a cyberattack. No outside source disputes this.

connection_assessment.reasoning: The FBI has not said how its database was hit or who did it. USDA called its problem a cyberthreat but named no attacker. Microsoft blamed a software bug, and the Pakistan cable fault has no stated cause. No official source links any of these, and AP says it saw no sign the FBI breach ties to the outages.
connection_assessment.would_change_my_mind: An official statement blaming the same attacker or company for the FBI and USDA incidents, or several big systems failing at the same moment.

alert.reason: Nothing new links the incidents. The FBI and USDA matters are still being investigated.

prep_note: No action is needed for most people. If you work with farm programs or law enforcement data, expect delays and check official agency pages for updates. Be careful with emails about USDA payments or FBI records, and use official websites. Check card payments if a game store fails.
